claims.explanation: Rivaroxaban is a factor Xa (F10) inhibitor that has no established direct cytotoxic anticancer mechanism; the selective killing pattern is most plausibly explained by F10 expression in the cancer lines, since lines with high F10 (factor Xa) expression would be expected to bind/respond to the drug more than F10-low lines. The observed pattern is noisy and the listed mutations (TP53, KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, etc.) are common pan-cancer drivers without a clear link to coagulation, so they are weak predictors. The most defensible genomic feature is therefore F10 expression, with any additional features being speculative.

features.basis: Drug target is coagulation factor Xa (F10); high target expression is the most direct predicted determinant of rivaroxaban response
